key_insight: RLVR weight updates lie on an almost one-dimensional trajectory: a rank‑1 approximation of the parameter deltas captures the majority of downstream performance gains, so you can estimate a single direction and extrapolate improvements with minimal RLVR training.
problem_solved: Reduces the cost, instability and opacity of full RLVR fine‑tuning by revealing a simple, low‑rank geometric structure that lets practitioners get most benefits from far fewer RL steps.
method: Collect parameter deltas from short RLVR runs and compute a low‑rank decomposition (top singular vector / principal direction).
Approximate the full trajectory with a rank‑1 direction and a scalar magnitude; use that direction to extrapolate larger effective updates or to apply minimal scalar tuning.
Validate extrapolated models on downstream reasoning tasks to show rank‑1 captures most performance gains and generalizes across checkpoints.
impact: Enables much cheaper, faster and more interpretable RL‑style improvements for LLMs: estimate one direction from a small RL run and scale it to obtain near‑equivalent gains without extensive RL training. This lowers compute, speeds iteration, and simplifies deployment.
visual_elements: Line/trajectory plot in high‑dimensional parameter space projected to 2D showing long curved path collapsing onto a single straight direction (rank‑1).
Bar or cumulative energy chart of singular values showing the first singular value dominates (rank‑1) and later values are negligible.
Performance vs. scale plot showing small RL run → extract direction → extrapolate magnitude → close-to-full RL performance.
Icon set: stopwatch/compute chip (cost savings), magnifying glass on a line (interpretability), arrow scaling a model (extrapolation)
paper_title: You Only Need Minimal RLVR Training: Extrapolating LLMs via Rank-1 Trajectories
paper_authors: Zhepei Wei, Xinyu Zhu, Wei-Lin Chen, Chengsong Huang, Jiaxin Huang
